_comment: Which files imply which scenarios, and whether frozen fixtures can even SEE the
change. `iterate start` consults this so the target stops being a flag you have to
remember, and `iterate end` re-checks it against what you actually touched.
The rule that matters: target 'live' means the offline UI serves this behavior from
a frozen fixture, so an offline capture would show your change as 'unchanged'. That
is a false negative — the worst outcome for this tool — so live wins any tie.
Patterns are fnmatch against repo-relative paths. Add rules as the app grows; an

rules.why: shared presentation — any tab can shift, but nothing about it needs Db2
Demo tab renders from demo_fixtures.json offline
Evaluate tab renders frozen numbers from eval_fixtures.json offline
shared shell: nav, tab switching, result cards. Touches every tab, so capture broadly
the Label tab has no offline path — pool building calls the backend
topic generation needs its own llama-server; there is no frozen fixture for it
the fixtures ARE the offline behavior; capturing offline is the point
retrieval + fusion. Offline serves frozen results, so it would show your change as unchanged
the reranker runs outside Db2, downstream of search — only visible live
metrics are computed by the backend; the offline tab shows a frozen snapshot
query understanding runs in the request path
the API only exists live; offline never calls it
corpus and judgments change what the engine returns, not what the page looks like

default.why: no rule matched — not known to affect the UI
